items.title: Somalia and Italy Together for Fisheries and the Blue Economy
items.description: (ANSA) - NAIROBI, 12 AGO - The Italian Ambassador to Somalia, Pier Mario Daccò Coppi, met with the Minister of Fisheries and the Blue Economy, Ahmed Hassan Adan, to receive an update on ongoing programs and exchange views on the prospects for a greater Italian presence in the sector. The Somali minister thanked Italy for funding the cooperation project aimed at strengthening the fisheries supply chain in the city of Bosaso (Puntland), expressing the hope that this initiative could be replicated in other locations across Somalia to contribute to the development of coastal communities. Minister
items.titleIt: Somalia and Italy Together for Fisheries and the Blue Economy

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.

items.title: Worries grow over mysterious illness killing Kenyan elephants
items.description: Worries over the death of elephants are mounting in southern Kenya, where at least 19 animals have died since June from an unexplained condition. With symptoms including partial paralysis, conservationists and communities are demanding urgent investigations into what is killing the elephants.
items.titleIt: Worries grow over mysterious illness killing Kenyan elephants

items.title: Ethiopia: Five Detained Ethiopian Journalists Pressured to Admit Terrorism Involvement in Exchange for Release, CPJ Says
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has called on Ethiopian authorities to release five journalists who have been detained for about three years while awaiting trial, alleging that they are being pressured to admit involvement in an armed insurgency and apologize in exchange for their freedom.
